instructions: StationGod reads and changes a running Stationeers world. Each tool is a verb; most take what (the kind of thing) and share option names: find (lists), inspect (one thing in detail), survey (an area or network), read (live values), write (set values), plan (work out, change nothing), check (rules), build, swap (existing pieces), remove, move, trade, show (draw for the player), undo, server. help {verb, what} gives one in full. Targets: id (one, a list, or a ref "r3" from an earlier reply), near + radius, box, room, network. 'this', 'that' or 'here' is the thing the crosshair is on: inspect {what: "looking_at"}. Typed ids act at once; build, swap, remove, trade, undo and cheats report until confirm: true, and so does any write given a ref, network or spread; ask the user before a cheat. Shaping on every verb: fields, omit, list_limits, output_file, repeat (a ref: that call again), whole: true (lifts the 12 KB cut). For waits, polls and timed or repeated work, run_script; for many targets, give id a list. A script changes nothing unless the run has confirm: true. If the user says stop or hold: server {what: 'stop'} (load the server tool if it isn't).

id.description: Target: an id, a list of ids, or a ref ("r3": the ids that reply showed).

rows.description: Rows each list of the report shows (0 for none); everything is still counted and checked.

near.description: Centre: [x, y, z], "player", "looking_at" or a thing's id (its position); with radius.

within.description: Only things inside this holder, at any depth.

box.description: Two corners [[x, y, z], [x, y, z]].

network.description: A network: its id, a piece or device on it, or {id, port}.

prefab.description: Prefab: a whole name, a hash, or parts with * ('*Battery*', '*Tank*Insulated*': each part, any order); or a list of them.

name.description: Part of the shown name or label, any case.

limit.x-script: The first n in order (entries); left out, every one.

cursor.description: open on a first page: keep the rest under a cursor when more follows (cursor_id); a cursor_id a page answered: the walk's next page.

include.description: Parts to add to the reply.

verbose.description: The long form of the reply.

gateway.description: "world" (default) or a gateway id: only devices on its data networks.

confirm.description: true does it; left out, the call only reports what it would do.

queue.description: Wait in line behind a running job (up to 8) instead of answering busy.

max_wait.description: Seconds to wait for a confirmed job to finish before answering; 0 answers with its job id at once.

materials.description: Holder(s) that pay materials and take source refunds, tried in order; ids or "player". Default the player.

refund_to.description: Where removed materials go: a word (inventory, source, storage, ground, none), a container id, or a list tried in turn.

acknowledge_gas_lost.description: The job id whose gas loss you accept (with the user's agreement); lifts the gas hold.

fields.description: Keys to keep in each entry (dotted paths go deeper).

list_limits.description: {list: count}: keep more of a list cut by default.

output_file.description: true or a file name: the whole reply to a file, answered by a pointer.

whole.description: No 4 KB cut; pages stay pages (limit, offset).

repeat.description: A ref ("r7"): run that call again, the options given here replacing its own; then what and the other options may be left out.

from_plan.description: A ref of a plan route or plan spot reply ("r9"; one spot: "r9.spots.2", default the first): build its build_arguments; options given here are added.

types.Color: {index: int | None, name: str | None, is_default: bool}
types.Thing: {reference_id: str, prefab_name: str | None, display_name: str | None}
types.Error: {code: str, message: str, data: Any | None, see: {verb: str | None, what: str | None, topic: str | None, subtopic: str | None} | None}

topics.errors: A refusal is {code, message, fix}: message says what went wrong, fix what to do next; a fix never names an allow value. Missing or wrong options are one invalid_argument listing every problem: {code, message, problems: [{path, problem}], valid: [this what's own options, the nearest 3 first]}. write logic with no target is missing_target, naming id and writes. Every message uses verb names. game_unavailable: the MCP server could not reach the game; a write may have run if the game took the call.
topics.paging: A list answers one page: limit entries from offset, with total and has_more. Next page: repeat: "r3" with offset. order: nearest (default) or id (pages stay put). Every reply ends with truncated. Report lists use rows, not limit: rows is how many entries each list of a report shows, never a page. whole: true lifts the 4 KB cut only; it never fetches more pages. Each what's own limit maximum is in its help.
topics.positions:
A point is [x, y, z] or {x, y, z} in world metres, +y up. Building tools snap it to the cell it falls in: 0.5 m small cells for pieces and small devices, 2 m large cells for frames, walls and large structures; the reply's resolved says where it landed. Where a what's at says so, it also takes:
- "looking_at": where the player's look ray hits within 10 m. {looking_at: true, right, up, forward} moves it in the player's frame. Example: at: "looking_at".
- {relative_to, frame, right, up, forward, anchor}: a point beside a thing. relative_to takes "player", "looking_at" or an id; frame player, world or target; anchor origin, top, bottom, left, right, front or back of its footprint. Example: at: {relative_to: "4820585", right: 2}.
- {on_face: true, along_right, along_up}: a point on the 2 m face plane you look at, right and up as you see them. Example: at: {on_face: true, along_right: 1}.
Every length is metres. no_crosshair_hit or no_face when the ray hits nothing; these need the player's view.
topics.refs:
Replies that are reports, plans, cut, or lists with has_more or 3 or more ids carry ref: "rN". The MCP server keeps the call and its whole reply until a world is loaded. A script run's id (script-14) is a ref to its returned value (sg.ref('script-14') in a script).
- As a target: id: "r3" is the ids that reply showed (see targets). A write whose target came from a ref reports first, with targets: {from, ids, more_in_source}.
- repeat: "r7" runs call r7 again, with the options you give replacing its own (what may be left out). repeat: "r7", confirm: true runs the report r7 for real on exactly the targets it listed. A plain repeat always calls the game; only a repeat that changes fields, omit or whole of a reply that is not a live value is answered from the store, marked from_store.
- from_plan: "r9" on build builds a plan route's or spot's build_arguments ("r9.spots.2": that spot).
topics.shaping:
The reply cap: a direct reply over 12 KB (some whats set their own threshold, named in their help) to a call that asked for no size is cut to about 4 KB; a report, whole: true, output_file, a paging limit above the default and list_limits are never cut. A cut reply keeps as much as fits, in this order: whole entries of its main list; else every entry in a shallow form (plain values kept, nested lists as their length, small objects kept, others as {...}); else the first shallow entries. With several lists, each is cut in proportion. It adds ref, cut ("8384 B; cells 4 of 8 shallow, pieces 9 of 18 shallow") and next: whole: repeat 'r4' with whole: true (~2620 tokens) | page: repeat 'r4' with offset: 8 | as a target, r4 is the shown entries.
fields [keys]: keep only these keys; a dotted path goes deeper. omit [paths]: leave keys out. list_limits {list: n}: keep more of a list cut by default. output_file: true or a file name: the whole reply to a file, answered by a pointer. Unknown fields names come back in fields_unmatched with fields_closest. Errors are never cut or shaped.
topics.targets:
Every verb names what it acts on the same way.
- id: one id, a list of ids, or a ref, where a what takes them (its help says; a what that takes one id says "One id"). A ref is the ids an earlier reply showed you: "r3" (its main list: the page, or the shown entries of a cut reply), "r3.members", "r4.rockets.parts" (a path through lists), "r9.spots.2" (one entry). For more than was shown, repeat the call with a larger limit. Any thing id may be "looking_at" (the thing the crosshair is on); "player" where a what says so. A rocket id may be its name ('Tanker').
- A list of ids where one is expected answers {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, payload | error}], count, success_count, error_count}, payload the one-id reply (a what with its own row keys says so); fields name payload keys. A typed list past the handler's maximum is refused, naming it.
- near + radius: around [x, y, z], "player", "looking_at" or a thing's id (its position), radius in metres. Each what says what near left out means; radius without near, or near "player" without radius, is refused.
- box: two corners [[x, y, z], [x, y, z]]. room: a room id. network: a network id, a piece or device on it, or {id, port}.
- prefab: a whole name, a hash (an integer, or a string of digits), or parts with *, each part matched in any order ('*Battery*', '*Tank*Insulated*'); or a list, any of which matches. A name or pattern that matches nothing answers prefab_not_found with the 3 nearest.
- name: part of the shown name or label, any case (a * in it is ignored). Players are named with player and to_player.
Lengths are metres and times seconds; other units are in the option's name.
topics.writes:
build, swap, remove, trade buy and sell, undo, and every cheat only report until confirm: true. move item by typed ids acts at once (a merge into another stack is [cannot undo]). A write given ids you typed out acts at once; a write whose targets you did not type out (a ref, a network, a spread) reports until confirm: true, listing every target with its current value under targets. Every report, direct or scripted, carries report_only: true. A report is never cut; its problems, warnings, will_burst, gas_check, passed and targets stay whatever fields or omit say. A report too large for the client answers report_too_large with the target count and how to narrow it.
Bulk work goes in one call, as wide as its options allow: the call's own schema bounds each list (placements 64, paint items 256, label labels 64, logic writes 256, memory values 512, remove cells and waypoints 1024) and a list over its bound is refused as invalid_argument; nothing is split. A confirmed bulk write is undone as write-N.
Jobs (build, swap, remove, undo) run one at a time; queue (default true) waits in line. A confirmed job, or gas move, answers when it is done, up to max_wait seconds (default 30, at most your client's timeout), with held_ms (how long it paused the game); after that it answers its id: inspect {what: "job", id}. Nothing fills in a default for you.
Undo: undo {id} takes back a build or removal job; swap jobs cannot be undone. A bulk write's undo takes back the steps marked [undo] in its report, newest first, one step at a time; it stops at a refused step, and from_step goes on.
Cheats change the world as a player cannot: move gas and player, write memory, battery and genes, server command (read-only commands too), build blueprint, free: true, force: true. Ask the user before each.
allow: [names] lifts a named guard for this call: door_keepout, split, contents, breach, broken, burst, unsupported, in_use, ground, off_network, out_of_range, overwrite, pad, lint. A call that lifted a guard lists the codes it passed in passed. A build that pays from the player's inventory warns materials_from_player. A write or report on a device that a chip, logic writer, screen script or another run drives warns driven_by (inspect controllers). A write that turns on or opens a vent, valve or pump is refused on a network lint problem unless allow: ["lint"].
topics.scripts:
A run is one call of verb calls: sg.<verb>('what', **options) is the direct call, with the same options and reply dicts, except that per-id whats always answer {results: [...]}, given one id or a list. Scripts are for waits, polls, timed or repeated writes and act-wait-act; for many targets a direct call with an id list is enough. A script changes nothing unless the run has confirm: true; confirm inside the code is refused.
- Seen (one rule for every write target, acted on or paid from): ids the MCP server sent you this session (replies after the cut, report rows, and a finished run's printed or returned value within its cut); int or str constants in the code, f-string pieces included (a target passes when its value equals one of them); selectors written in the code (a network, a spread, sg.ref('r7')); what this run builds; "player". The seen set is shared by every agent on this MCP server.
- Report run: run_script {code}. Nothing changes. Every target is listed as [id or cell, name, current -> new], with its undo mark, warnings and lifted guards; a build names a piece it would place by its cell (it has no id yet) and counts them in the report's placed, changed and kept (a confirmed job's log.placed names each). Waits are real until the first write; after a write, the second wait inside a while or watch loop ends the pass with a BaseException, so finally runs and is reported; finite for loops run through. One header line gives the limits. To act, send the same code again with confirm: true: the report's rows are now seen.
- Confirmed run: run_script {code, confirm: true}. Acts as it goes on seen targets. An unseen target stops the run with sg.Stopped (a BaseException). The reply says whether anything acted, lists the refused call's targets as rows (now seen), and gives the fix: "nothing acted: send it again with confirm: true", or "these acted: [...]; undo script-N first, then send it again". A stopped run is not resumed.
- After a stop (server stop, a write-rule stop, a user cancel or a world change), held restores and logic writes to targets the run already wrote still act, footered CLEANUP, until the kill (5 s after the stop, longer while a call is in flight, never past 30 s, or on a second stop). Writes to other targets answer an error row and do not raise, so the rest of finally runs. Waits do not raise after a stop. After a world change nothing acts.
- Restores: with sg.hold(id, logic, value=None, after=<value before>): registers after with the mod first, then writes value, and restores on exit; the mod also applies it at session end or after an unresumed disconnect, in the same world, while the target still holds the run's last written value. id may be a list; logic writes only. finally is best effort: it runs on stops and run ends, but not when the session ends.
- Waiting: sg.wait(s); time.sleep is sg.wait. Poll a sensor with read (a room or find query walks the world). sg.watch(reads, until, timeout) -> (rows, met): reads are read logic reads entries; until(rows) gets the rows in order; it never raises at timeout; it subscribes where the devices topic covers the reads and otherwise polls, 1 s for a light read and 5 s for one that asks atmosphere; in a report run it returns (current rows, True). sg.changes(reads, timeout, every=1) yields the read rows on each change; every, the sampling window in seconds, defaults to 1 and is never under 0.5 (one game tick); it never raises at the timeout and clears at stream end. sg.jobs(timeout) yields one item per job the run started that ends, the job object its job_ended event carries; it never raises at the timeout and clears at stream end.
- Composition: from sg.lib import <name> loads a saved script as a module (its main is callable), and sg.script(name)(**args) calls one; both are this one run, so the script's literals count as written and its writes, holds, stops and undo are the run's. A hub without --scripts-dir serves no saved scripts: the import is refused.
- A run is a job (script-N). A confirmed run answers within 30 s whatever max_wait says (max_wait may only shorten); a report or read-only run (no write or sg.hold in the code) waits up to the client's limit (600 s for Claude Code). A run past its reply answers script-N running: line 4, 37 s in, +3 write logic, 1.8 calls/s, 0.4 ms/s game. Follow it with inspect {what: "job", id: "script-N"}.
- Stop: server {what: "stop", id} stops one run; with no id, every live run, answering the ids and first lines. The run gets sg.Stopped once. The stop reply lists left: (changed and not restored) and each job in flight.
- Notices name the run's id and first code line and end "if you did not start it, leave it". A done notice comes on run_script and inspect job replies. A run that left something is one sticky left: line on every reply until you inspect it by id.
- Undo: undo {id: "script-N"} reverts the whole run, newest first, to the values before it. A target changed since the run's last write is reported and not written unless allow: ["overwrite"]. Undo of a running run is refused. After a world change: undo_expired.
- Calls: script calls mint no refs and are never cut. Iterating a reply dict raises TypeError naming its main list; a single for walks the main list by cursor, and len, an index, sorted or a second pass page in the rest. offset is refused; limit is the first n in order. A script call waits for its job.
- Errors raise sg.Error(code, message, fix, maybe_ran); only write-rule stops and stops are sg.Stopped. A failed run's reply gives the line and its source, the exception, the sg call with its code and fix, a reply dict's keys (nearest first), the values on the line, then the footer.
- The reply: state; returned value (return x or a final bare expression, 4 KB cut); printed output (4 KB cut); then the footer: writes by outcome, WARNINGS (driven_by, lint), PASSED, CONTESTED (a written value found changed), CLEANUP, undo with the classes, and the cost line (calls, calls/s, writes, game ms and ms/s, frames over budget, samples and their ms, updates, tick held, wall time).

What run replies look like:
script-14 done
returned: {'start_kpa': 2101.5, 'end_kpa': 8004.2}
DONE write logic x2 (4612280 Open)
undo script-14 (logic writes [undo])
cost script-14 (ff = '4612280'): 243 calls, 1.0 calls/s, 2 writes, 6.2 game ms (0.03 ms/s), 0 frames over budget, 0 samples, 0.0 ms sampling, 0 updates, held tick 0 ms, 251 s wall

script-15 REPORT: nothing changed; send the code again with confirm: true to act
limits: reads after a reported write show the old value; a waiting loop runs once; writes on what this run builds are not shown
REPORTED write logic x3 [undo]:
  [4701001, Wall Light 1, On 1 -> 0]
  [4701002, Wall Light 2, On 1 -> 0]
  [4701007, Wall Light (hall), On 1 -> 0]

script-18 stopped: unseen target at line 9 (3 targets, now seen); these acted: [4170302 On]; undo script-18 first, then send it again
DONE write logic x1 (4170302 On)
left: 4170302 On=0, set line 2
topics.types: Shared reply types. The small ones (Thing, Vec3, Error, Color, LogicType) are written out on the Types line of each stub that uses them. Job views come one per call: help {topic: "types", subtopic: "<name>"} or sg.help('types', '<name>'). Names: BuildJob, GasCheck, JobBusy, JobQueued, JobDropped, RefundPlan, RunJob, SwapJob, UpgradeJob.
